label: thm:wedderburn-mass-formula
title: Three-invariant atomic mass formula
html:
Let (Z, N) be a neutral atom with atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{A+Z}(q) (atomic braid). For each generator i of the braid, let M_i denote the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix obtained by chaining the crossing matrices of all strands j > i. Then the atomic mass is

  \mathfrak{m}(Z, N)
  =
  Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}}
  + N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}}
  + Z \cdot m_e
  + \alpha\bigl(
      \Phi_1
      - 2[3]_q \cdot \Phi_2
      + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3
    \bigr)

where:

  \Phi_1 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert
    z \cdot (M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}
  \bigr\rvert,
  \qquad
  \Phi_2 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert
    \det M_i
  \bigr\rvert,
  \qquad
  \Phi_3 = \sum_i \ln\left\lvert
    \frac{\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}}
         {\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}}
  \right\rvert.

The three invariants correspond to the three Wedderburn blocks of H_n(R, q):

Invariant Wedderburn block Matrix quantity
\Phi_1 standard (dim n{-}1) trace of Markov-weighted product
\Phi_2 sym \times alt determinant (product of eigenvalues)
\Phi_3 sym / alt ratio of eigenvalues (chirality)

The three invariants correspond to the three extremal Wedderburn blocks of H_n(R, q) (those associated with the symmetric [n], standard [n{-}1,1], and alternating [1^n] representations). These three extremal blocks exhaust the partition lattice if and only if n \le 3 (p(1)=1, p(2)=2, p(3)=3); already at n = 4 (p(4)=5), two non-extremal blocks [2,2] and [2,1,1] enter, and for A \ge 3 nucleons the adjacent-chain bridge count A - 1 grows strictly slower than the all-pairs count A(A-1)/2. The partition-by-partition computation (the formal derivation) computes all partitions exactly via Young's seminormal form in polynomial time. The mass functional uses the three extremal invariants as the leading-order formula; the full partition sum gives the exact Markov trace.

The coefficients are:

  • \alpha = m_e \times 8G (binding scale),
  • [3]_q = (q^3 - q^{-3})/(q - q^{-1}), the quantum 3-integer,
  • h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1}, the Hecke parameter, satisfying the exact algebraic dependency h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 = [3]_q - 3, i.e. 2\beta_3 + \beta_2 + 6 = 0 where \beta_2 = -2[3]_q and \beta_3 = h_{\mathrm{A}}^2.

All quantities are derived from q_0 and m_e. The formula has zero fitted parameters.
